Malad Fish Market is a great place to buy fresh fish at good prices. You can get discounted rates if you buy in bulk, and bargaining skills definitely help here. There’s a wide variety of fresh seafood available, and the quality is good if you choose carefully.
The market can be crowded and busy, but that’s part of the experience. Best place for people who know how to negotiate and want value for money.

featured_reviews.name: ViSHAL SUTAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
1.	Freshness & Variety
•	Wide range of sea fish and also crabs.  ￼
•	Fish catches are fresh; many comment that it’s among the best places for seafood lovers.  ￼
2.	Value for money / Wholesale rates
•	Prices often more reasonable than smaller local shops, especially if you buy early or in bulk.  ￼
•	Ability to bargain.  ￼
3.	Additional services
•	Fish cleaning / cutting service available. Some vendors provide cleaning without extra cost or for a small charge.  ￼
•	Open long hours—starting early in morning through most of the day.  ￼
4.	Location & accessibility
•	Near Malad Railway Station, so relatively easy for many people to reach.  ￼
5.	Atmosphere
•	“Vibe” of a genuine fish market: lively, bustling; people like the authenticity.

featured_reviews.review_text:
That's wonderful to hear! The Malad Fish Market in Mumbai is indeed very well-known for being a bustling, vibrant hub.
​It's famous for:
​Wholesale and Retail: It's a major market where you can buy a vast variety of fresh saltwater fish at both wholesale and retail prices.
​Variety of Seafood: You can find everything from prawns, pomfret, Bombay duck, and crabs, often straight from the catch.

featured_reviews.name: Sushil Malik
featured_reviews.review_text: Malad Fish Market is a large, busy seafood market in Malad West, just a short walk from Malad railway station (West) on Sainath Road, and is popular for fresh, relatively low-priced sea fish. Location and access Located on Sainath Road, very close to Malad Railway Station (West); it is  2–5 minutes from the station. Timings  roughly 6:00 am onwards; morning hours are the main time when the wholesale and freshest stock comes.Locals recommend going around 6:00–7:30 am if you want the best catch and prices, especially if buying in bulk. Market layout and what you getThe market is divided into multiple sections: unloading/wholesale area on the road, a covered retail area where they also clean and cut, and open sections where you buy and then pay extra at cutting counters. You typically get a wide variety of saltwater fish like pomfret, surmai, bangda, bombil, prawns, crabs and seasonal catch, with both retail and wholesale options. Tips for visiting Go early, carry change, and be ready to bargain hard; prices are better if you buy in larger quantities.It is a traditional wet market, so expect crowds, strong smell, and wet floors. simple washable footwear and carrying your own bags can be more comfortable.If you tell what exactly you want (pomfret, prawns, bulk/retail, specific budget),

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: priyanka mustafi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good food, quite authentic in taste. We had prawn manchow soup which was loaded with prawns. Their prawn lollypops are great, we also had squid tawa masala which was a bit salty but well cooked. We ordered thalis which was the main aim. Surmai and pomfret. The size was very good and fish was fresh. The thali was very good - rice, bhakri ( u can choose amboli or even chapati) , bhurji, sukka, prawn curry, bangda curry, salad and ofcourse rawa fry of the fish you choose. The place is very tiny with only 8 tables but service is prompt and nice ambience for a homely meal
.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

name: Mughal Dhaba
description: Welcome to Mughal Dhaba - the home of authentic Mughlai cuisine in Kurla. Our restaurant offers a unique dining experience, bringing the taste of Bhiwandi Dhaba to your city. Our menu features a variety of delicious dishes, cooked with traditional Mughlai spices and herbs, to satisfy your taste buds. Some of our main dishes are Channa Papad, Best starters, Biryani & Kebabs. Come visit us in Kurla, Mumbai and enjoy the best Mughlai flavors of our rich culinary heritage.

featured_reviews.name: Murtaza Kapasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
A wonderful dining experience overall. The ambience is genuinely impressive. It was clean, calm, and welcoming. The place is spacious, well‑maintained, and offers both family seating as well as a comfortable Majlis (Dastarkhan) area, which adds a traditional touch to the experience.
Parking is convenient too, with two‑wheeler space available and valet parking for four‑wheelers.

Every dish that we ordered were tasty:
• Bhiwandi Style Chana
• Cream Chicken Soup
• Chicken Arbi Kabab
• Manchurian Noodles

Overall, a great spot for families, groups, and anyone looking for delicious food with a pleasant atmosphere. Definitely worth visiting again.

featured_reviews.name: Mobin Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: MUGHAL DHABA is a great spot if you’re craving authentic Mughlai flavors with a true dhaba vibe. The food is rich, flavorful, and generously portioned. Their gravies are perfectly spiced, not overpowering, and you can tell the dishes are cooked fresh Service is quick and friendly, and the staff is polite and attentive. The ambience is simple and no-frills, exactly what you expect from a dhaba, but clean and welcoming Overall, Mughal Dhaba is excellent value for money and a solid choice for family dinners or casual outings with friends.THANK YOU😊

Pure khane mein bas a rahi thi Ande ka chhilka Mila very bad experience don't order and don't waste your money

featured_reviews.name: empire realinfra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Great service,wowwww food and loved the ambience 🤍
Shoutout to shannu sir great service and hospitality.

featured_reviews.name: Sahil Pagui
featured_reviews.review_text: The restaurant ambience was truly impressive, with a beautiful Mughlai setup that added a rich cultural touch to the dining experience. The place was very clean and hygienic, and the food was excellent in both taste and quality. Overall, a wonderful experience — highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Saniya Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Service was really nice. Everyone was very sweet and staff was always available. I read all the bad reviews and I was really skeptical. But when I went there it was an amazing experience. We had a lot of food and it was worth the price.
Chicken lollipop 5/5
Behrateen chicken 2/5
Mutton handi 5/5
Chicken Dabang 4/5
Paneer Kadai 1/5
Jeera Rice 4/5 quantity was less
Julab Jamun 2/5 not tasty
My mom really liked the chicken lollipop

featured_reviews.name: Shoeb Surve
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently dined at Mughal Dhaba, and the experience was delightful. The pasta was cooked to perfection, with rich, authentic flavors that transported me straight to Dhaba style foods. The ambiance was warm and inviting, making it a perfect spot for a cozy dinner. The service was attentive without being intrusive, and the tiramisu was the perfect sweet ending to a fantastic meal. My only complaint is that the biryani can be more better in taste compare to other items in Nawabi Thaal. Overall, a great place to enjoy Italian cuisine with friends or family.  😋  😋  😋  😋  😋

featured_reviews.name: Maahi Ashrafi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mughal Dhaba and had a wonderful experience! The food was absolutely delicious — authentic Mughlai flavors, rich gravies, and perfectly cooked dishes that truly captured the essence of traditional Mughlai cuisine. Every bite was full of flavor and aroma.
The restaurant also deserves appreciation for its cleanliness and hygiene. The dining area was spotless, and the overall environment felt fresh and well-maintained. The staff was courteous, attentive, and quick with service, which made the experience even better.
If you’re a fan of Mughlai food, I highly recommend Mughal Dhaba. It’s one of the best places for mouth-watering Mughlai dishes and a clean, comfortable dining experience!
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

featured_reviews.name: Shishir Deshpande
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent place for FreshCatch especially if one lands up there around 8/8:30 am or thereabouts. The fish comes off the boats around 5 am or so and lands up at the Versova Village Fish Market by 8 am.
One can really bargain here and get fresh fish for reasonable prices, having said that ‘reasonable’ is really relative as seafood due to over fishing and environmental challenges has become quite expensive.
A must visit for seafood lovers for a home cooked meal!!

featured_reviews.name: Gupta Rohit
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a nice place for fish/prawns buying. Market starts at 7 AM. You have to be tough negotiator here. Do not be in rush to buy, there are plenty of options, be careful while buying, there are chances you may be robbed of old fishes. You can get all the items chopped and cleaned, there are seperate people who cleans it up for you. I came across the cleaning chopping lady Gauri, if you are a noob in buying she can help you with good buy. If you have more time you can visit Bhau cha Dhakka but than it takes more to travel and you will have to be early bird and experienced to negotiate and have good find.

featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text: Nice place for fish. But please bargain.

featured_reviews.name: Ganesh Patkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Fresh fish available here, one must know how to bargain.

featured_reviews.name: vipul chamur (OFFICIAL VIPUL)
featured_reviews.review_text: Versova koli wada is nice with culture fisheries local womens selling fish while their husband or male person going for fishing  at sea. As they called them sagar devta as well as their  typical local language koli sounds so good.

featured_reviews.name: Shishir Deshpande
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent for fresh sea food and sea food lovers who like cooking. A wide variety of fresh catch is available with fish like Pomphrets, Prawns / Shrimps, Crabs, lobsters et al.
The fresh catch comes every alternate day from the aversive jetty where the trawlers arrive every alternate days or so.
It’s a historical place in its own way.

featured_reviews.name: asif sharief shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: Very good place for holesale fish in all variety

featured_reviews.name: Salim Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: Fish market at Andheri west Versova. You need to have good bargain skills to buy anything from here. The sellers are quite humble and polite,  but also be ready to get insulted if you are trying to bargain at a very low price below the expected lowest price and when you irritate them. Don't get emotionally carried away with the stories the sellers might try to sell. They will never sell even at their cost price. And the term 'bony karo' will be heard a lot. Don't get carried away. They will never give away unless they make profits. Generally the fishes are quite fresh and good to eat. The quantity matters for a good deal.

featured_reviews.name: Manish Dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a good place if you need to buy fish in large quantities. You will find fresh & good quality of Prawns, Surmai, Pomfret, Bangda & Bombayduck. Make sure to be there between 8AM to 9:30AM. Because after this time it is the small retailers who sell there. And if you want to get the fish cleaned : de-shelling the prawns, cleaning Bombayduck etc. you can get it done from small errand boys and girls who will do it for 30-50 Rs. Also be prepared to dare thru some fish slurry on the floor and ofcourse the STRONG  stench of fish.
